title: Flat isotrivial degenerations of hyperbolic toric Kato manifolds with toric central fibre and boundary gluing
difficulty_reason: Allow standard toric orbit/fan dictionaries, the paper toric universal-cover realization, the reused Kato fundamental-domain construction, and the named flatness criterion. The remaining construction chooses an admissible primitive u and lattice v, designs the lifted lattice automorphisms and periodic fans, and constructs invariant open domains whose quotient has the prescribed nonzero fibres and the central toric boundary identification E-prime~H-prime. Compatibility of the parameter, deck action, changing fan and boundary gluing is the joint H2 burden; standard Cohen-Macaulay/equidimensional flatness alone is not the burden. The Nakamura construction and its isotrivial variant share this one template and are counted once. Subsequent log-cohomology, residue and classification calculations are retained without a second independent H2 count.

problems.title: Projectivity of the compactified ball modification when a Kato manifold has Kähler universal cover
problems.difficulty_reason: Miyaoka extension and Moishezon projectivity do not transfer the universal-cover Kahler form to the modified ball on their own. Proposition2.4 constructs compatible holomorphic embeddings by iterating the Kato fundamental domains and proving that they exhaust the punctured modified ball. Lemma10.2 then glues the pulled-back form to a Fubini–Study multiple through a controlled regularized maximum, providing the new construction needed before the final projectivity theorem applies.

problems.difficulty_reason: The proof turns an arbitrary-dimensional Laurent mutation into explicit Newton-slice polyhedra and an integral admissible Minkowski pair for a torus-equivariant deformation. It then identifies the mutated cone through the two tailcone inclusions and checks the degree-zero projectivization needed for a flat projective family over P1. The full construction is beyond a toric fan definition check; the previously established p-divisor family theorem is used only after these new coefficients are supplied.
